one_liner: Senior DISA acquisition and portfolio analyst at Fort Meade who advises the Component Acquisition Executive on major defense IT program reviews, budgets (PPBE), and business cases.
fit_summary: This is a GS-15 executive-level role that requires a year of GS-14-equivalent experience leading major program analyses, managing program resources, or defending program plans and funding to senior stakeholders, plus SCI clearance eligibility. Daniel's IEM consulting background and policy knowledge are relevant to stakeholder coordination, but nothing on file shows senior acquisition, budget, or PPBE leadership at that level. Unless Daniel led large federal program analyses or resource management at IEM, this is unlikely to qualify, and a GS-9 to GS-12 analyst role is a better target.
eligibility: Open to the public under DoD Direct Hire Authority (5 USC 9905); veterans' preference does not apply, and you do not need federal status.

Requires one year of specialized experience equivalent to GS-14 in at least one area: leading analytical studies of major programs, resource management covering two or more of cost analysis, budget formulation, contract management, or strategic resource planning, or representing an organization to justify or defend programs and resources with senior stakeholders.
Requires eligibility for a Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) clearance, which means a TS/SCI investigation.
There is no education substitution at GS-15, so experience must carry the qualification on its own. Qualifications must be met within 30 days after the closing date.
strategy: Before applying, check honestly whether your IEM work included leading program evaluations, managing budgets or contracts, or briefing senior government officials at a level comparable to GS-14. If it did not, skip this posting and target GS-11/12 program or management analyst roles at FEMA, DHS, or Virginia VDEM.

If you do apply, describe IEM work in terms of the specialized experience areas, for example disaster recovery program evaluations, grant or cost analysis, and recommendations to government clients. Name the scale (dollar amounts, number of programs) only where true.
Address all four listed competencies within the body of a two-page resume, giving dates and hours per week for each job. No separate KSA statement is required.
Preview the questionnaire at the USA Staffing link and answer conservatively. The agency checks answers against your resume, and inflated ratings can cost you consideration.
The window runs only October 22–30, 2026, so have your resume and any transcripts ready before it opens.
resume_bullets: Led [number] analytical studies evaluating [type of disaster recovery/preparedness program] for [government client], developing recommendations adopted in [plan/policy].
Performed cost analysis and budget formulation for [program] totaling [$ amount], tracking [contract/grant] execution against [requirements].
Briefed and negotiated program plans and resource needs with [senior client officials/agency leaders] across [number] federal, state, and local partners.
interview_questions: Describe a time you defended a program's funding or resources to senior leaders who were skeptical.
How have you built a Business Case Analysis or evaluated alternative courses of action under risk?
How would you align competing program requirements across multiple stakeholder organizations with an agency's mission goals?
What experience do you have with PPBE or federal budget cycles?
watch_outs: The GS-15 level makes it likely you will be found not qualified without senior program, budget, or acquisition leadership experience.
The SCI clearance requirement means a lengthy investigation, and offers are contingent on clearance eligibility.
The application window is only nine days.
Fort Meade, Maryland is a long commute from Manassas; telework is allowed but the job is not remote.
